title: Radiant Back Hand Bracelet Cuff Mehndi Design for Finger
descriptionParagraphs: A graceful back hand mehndi design designed for the fingers, featuring checkered fill and spiral rosette. Rated as Hard, this pattern is perfect for a party.

Finger designs are quick to apply and dry fast, which makes them practical when time is short. Fingertips have thicker skin, so the stain there usually develops darker than on the rest of the hand. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.

The back of the hand is the most visible placement for mehndi because it shows whenever the hands are at rest. Arabic-style trails that run diagonally from the index finger to the wrist are one of the most popular back-hand layouts.

Application tips: Dab a lemon and sugar mixture on the dried paste to keep it moist and stuck to the skin. Scrape the dried paste off instead of washing it, and keep the area away from water for the first 12 to 24 hours.

image.alt: Back Hand Bracelet Cuff mehndi design for finger — radiant henna pattern

faq.q: How long does back-hand mehndi last?
faq.a: Usually about one to two weeks, a little less than the palm, since the back of the hand is washed and exposed more.

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?
faq.a: A natural henna stain usually lasts one to three weeks. It fades faster on areas that are washed or rubbed often, such as the hands.

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.
